title: Enhanced RNA extraction for diverse tissues
author: Damaris Godinez-Vidal
materials: Quantify and analyze the total RNA (Note 6).

steps.title: Take safety precautions
steps.instruction: Wear closed‑toe shoes, appropriate clothing, protective goggles, and gloves before handling detergents and solvents.

steps.title: Clean work area
steps.instruction: Wipe the bench or work surface with 70 % ethanol and place paper towels nearby.

steps.title: Prepare RNA extraction buffer
steps.instruction: Prepare the appropriate buffer: use Z6 buffer for soft plant vegetative or reproductive tissue (e.g., frozen leaves) and GS buffer for hard tissue (woody roots), plant seeds, fresh fungal mycelia, nematodes, and arthropods. Add 360 µL β‑mercaptoethanol to 50 mL of the chosen buffer, mix, then cool before use. Store the buffer at room temperature if not in use.

steps.title: Cool the buffer
steps.instruction: Keep the GS buffer on ice or at 4 °C until needed.

steps.title: Grind frozen tissue
steps.instruction: Using liquid nitrogen, grind 100 mg of frozen tissue (or enough powder to fill 100 µL of the Eppendorf tube; up to 200 µL powder if the GS buffer volume is increased to 500 µL). Transfer the powder to an Eppendorf tube, add the cooled GS buffer, hold the tube by the top or cap, keep the tube on ice, and vortex for no more than two seconds. If the buffer freezes, keep the sample on ice until vortexed.

steps.title: Add phenol‑chloroform (first extraction)
steps.instruction: While the tubes remain on ice, open them and add 1 volume phenol:chloroform (1:1 v/v). Vortex for no more than two seconds, return to ice, and vortex again until the suspension turns white.

steps.title: Centrifuge first extraction
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the suspension at 12,000 rpm for 10 min at 4 °C.

steps.title: Collect supernatant
steps.instruction: Label new Eppendorf tubes, keep them on ice, and carefully transfer the upper phase (supernatant) without touching the interphase to a new tube.

steps.title: Phenol‑chloroform wash
steps.instruction: Add an equal volume of phenol:chloroform (1:1 v/v) to the collected supernatant, vortex briefly, and centrifuge at 12,000 rpm for 10 min at 4 °C. Repeat the “Collect supernatant” and “Phenol‑chloroform wash” steps until the white interface disappears or becomes completely transparent (typically three washes for young leaf, nematode or arthropod tissue; four washes for woody roots, seeds, or fungal mycelia).

steps.title: Final aqueous phase recovery
steps.instruction: Label new tubes, keep them on ice, and transfer the clear upper phase to a fresh tube without disturbing any residual interphase.

steps.title: Precipitate RNA
steps.instruction: Add an equal volume of cold absolute isopropanol and add 1/10 volume of 3 M sodium acetate (pH 5.2) (e.g., for 600 µL total volume add 60 µL acetate). Incubate for 30–40 min at –20 °C (if tissue <30 mg, incubation may be extended to 3 h; if tissue ≥100 mg, avoid incubation longer than 60 min).

steps.title: Pellet RNA
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at 14,000 rpm for 15 min at 4 °C.

steps.title: Wash pellet with 500 µL ethanol
steps.instruction: Add 500 µL cold absolute ethanol, vortex until the pellet detaches from the tube bottom, then centrifuge at 14,000 rpm for 7 min at 4 °C.

steps.title: Wash pellet with 200 µL ethanol
steps.instruction: Add 200 µL absolute ethanol and centrifuge at 14,000 rpm for 7 min at 4 °C.

steps.title: Dry pellet
steps.instruction: Decant the ethanol using a plastic beaker and invert the tubes on a paper towel to dry the pellet for no more than 5 min.

steps.title: Resuspend RNA
steps.instruction: Add nuclease‑free water (no more than 30 µL; if the pellet is not visible, add 20 µL) and incubate the tubes at 65 °C for 10 min.
